text.p: Headlines from major national newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
EL PAIS
- One of leaders of "Y groups", violent youth groups that support ETA Basque Separatists, arrives in prison after being arrested on Friday in Pamplona.
- Treasury reduces income tax by 2.7 percent to boost consumption.
EL MUNDO
- Joaquin Leguina authorized payments from various organisations within Community of Madrid to various companies of Ferrer Europe group for studies that cannot be found.
- Basque radicals attack and set on fire Lagun bookshop in San Sebastian for fourth time.
- Government to ensure that those that cannot receive surgical treatment in public hospitals due to excess demand can go to private hospitals free of charge.
DIARIO 16
- Spanish footballers begin to voice their disgust before trade union AFE of how they feel usurped by foreign players in League.
- Real Madrid was not capable of winning against Extremadura in Spanish town Almendralejo.
ABC
- Prince Felipe will take part for first time in National Defence Board, presided by king.
CINCO DIAS
- On Spanish bourse, none of stocks that started 1997 as top performers appear among best performers at end of year.
- Olive oil producers warn that if cost price does not continue to fall there will be no other choice than to agree to sizeable imports from Tunisia, Turkey and Morocco.
EXPANSION
- Chairman of Madrid bourse says privatisations will increase turnover and stability of bourse.
- Construction and service group FCC buys transport company Aitena from BBV.
- Institute of Overseas Commerce anticipates increasing control over aid awarded to export companies.
GACETA DE LOS NEGOCIOS
- Treasury efforts to reduce income tax will be operational in February, will free 80 billion pesetas for consumption, and will release further 300,000 citizens from income tax payments.
- John de Zulueta, managing director of Sanitas, says main problem with state health care is there is no control on hospital spending. mad mcm
